item.title: American Airlines flight attendant's alleged killers tied to gang accused of preying on tourists: officials
item.description: Two suspects captured in Peru months after allegedly drugging and killing American Airlines flight attendant Eric Fernando Gutierrez Molina in Medellín.
item.content:encoded:
Two men accused of drugging and killing an American Airlines flight attendant during a layover in Colombia have been arrested months after the slaying, authorities said, with the suspects allegedly tied to a gang known to prey on tourists.

Andrés Felipe Peña Corrales, 23, and William Olave Gamboa, 31, were captured in Peru in connection with the March killing of Eric Fernando Gutierrez Molina, 32, a Dallas-based flight attendant whose disappearance in Medellín sparked an international search.

Peña Corrales has since been transferred to Colombia to face charges, while Olave Gamboa remains in Peruvian custody awaiting extradition proceedings. Both men face charges including aggravated homicide and aggravated robbery in Colombia, according to authorities.

AMERICANS WARNED POPULAR TRAVEL ROUTES THIS SUMMER COULD CARRY CRIME AND KIDNAPPING RISKS

A third suspect, María del Carmen González, 24, was arrested separately in Montería, Colombia. Investigators allege she was not directly involved in Gutierrez Molina’s killing but participated in withdrawing and moving money stolen from foreign victims as part of the group’s operation.

Colombian police identified all three suspects as alleged members of Los Goteros, a criminal organization accused of targeting foreign tourists by contacting them through dating apps, gaining their trust, drugging them and stealing money, jewelry and other valuables.

According to reporting by El Colombiano, investigators believe Gutierrez Molina was contacted through a dating app before meeting several people at a nightclub in Medellín’s El Poblado neighborhood.

The group later went to a hotel, where Gutierrez Molina and his coworker were allegedly drugged before their belongings were stolen and their financial accounts were accessed, the outlet reported.

The outlet also reported that scopolamine, sometimes called "Devil’s Breath" or "Dragon’s Breath," may have been used to incapacitate the victims, though authorities have not publicly confirmed toxicology findings in the case.

Gutierrez Molina was reportedly strangled, while his coworker survived.

DATING-APP CHARMER ACCUSED OF MURDER AFTER HISTORY OF DOMESTIC ARRESTS INVOLVING WOMEN HE MET ONLINE

Investigators allege the group accessed Gutierrez Molina’s bank accounts, stole other valuables and abandoned his body near Jericó, southwest of Medellín, where it was found five days later.

The arrests capped a months-long international investigation involving U.S. Homeland Security Investigations, Colombian prosecutors and Peruvian authorities.

"This successful outcome reflects the strong commitment of the United States, Colombia and Peru to work together to investigate and bring to justice a group of criminals in Colombia dedicated to the robbery and theft of U.S. citizens and ensure the safety of international travelers in the region," the U.S. Embassy in Colombia said in a joint statement.

The embassy also recognized the Mayor’s Office of Medellín, Colombia’s National Police and Peru’s National Police for their roles in the investigation.

EXCLUSIVE: ALLEGED $32M COVID-19 FRAUD FUGITIVE CAPTURED IN JAMAICA AND RETURNED TO US, FBI SAYS

Gutierrez Molina disappeared in March while on an overnight layover in Medellín before he was scheduled to continue to Miami.

Friends told local media at the time that he shared his location from an Airbnb near José María Córdova International Airport before communication suddenly stopped, prompting coworkers and family members to report him missing.

Days later, Medellín Mayor Federico Gutiérrez announced that authorities had recovered a body near Jericó. The remains were later identified as Gutierrez Molina.

"We are heartbroken by the tragic passing of our colleague," American Airlines said in a statement previously provided to Fox News Digital.

"Our thoughts and support are with his family, loved ones and colleagues during this difficult time, and we are doing all we can to assist Colombian law enforcement in its investigation."

Authorities said investigators are working to determine whether additional foreign tourists were victimized by Los Goteros using the same alleged scheme.

Fox News Digital's Alex Koch and Alex Nitzberg contributed to this report.

item.title: Clay Travis tells Dan Dakich about his $10 million offer to the Las Vegas Aces and how Elon Musk could help
item.description: Clay Travis explains his $10 million challenge to the Las Vegas Aces and suggests Elon Musk could raise the stakes to $100 million to force a response.
item.content:encoded:
OutKick founder Clay Travis set the WNBA and sports world on fire recently when he made a compelling financial and social offer to the league and its best team, the Las Vegas Aces.

Play a state championship-winning high school boys basketball team of his choice, with $10 million up for grabs should they win.

This offer presented a compelling opportunity for the WNBA and the Aces to meaningfully increase their revenue, should they win the game, and more importantly, live up to their stated ideology and political beliefs. When Sophie Cunningham said in an interview that she wanted to protect girls, prevent males from competing in women's sports and keep locker rooms exclusively female, the outrage from many prominent personalities around the league was fierce and immediate.

CLAY TRAVIS UPS OFFER TO $10 MILLION FOR WNBA CHAMPION LAS VEGAS ACES TO PLAY HIGH SCHOOL BOYS BASKETBALL TEAM

Players and coaches wore T-shirts expressing their support for males playing in women's sports. Her own coach said she wasn't educated on the science of males competing against women. A co-owner of the Seattle Storm was suspended for confronting young fans. And anti-biology WNBA fans have spent the past few Indiana Fever games booing Cunningham at every opportunity.

So far, though, both the league and the Aces have been dead silent when it comes to the golden opportunity Travis gave them. He joined "Don't @ Me with Dan Dakich" to talk about what led to the offer and how Elon Musk, of all people, could help.

CHERYL REEVE SENDS CLEAR MESSAGE TO SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM WITH ‘TRANS KIDS BELONG’ SHIRT DURING FEVER-LYNX GAME

"Sometimes the best way to respond to absurdity is to accept the absurd premise and advance it further to a larger degree of absurdity," Travis said. "Everyone with a functional brain knows that men are bigger, stronger and faster than women. And the whole reason women's sports exist is so women can compete because if we just had unisex sports, men would take all the spots and there would be no women's sports. So I said, as a way to point out this absurdity, I will give $10 million to a boys high school team, playing against WNBA champion Las Vegas Aces."

He also brought up that an even bigger dollar figure from someone with more resources, like Elon Musk, for example, could force the Aces hand.

"I would love it if somebody like Elon Musk would come in and say, 'hey, I'll make it 100 million,' you know. Because I think the dollar figure at 10 million, most people out there, if you thought you had a reasonable chance to win, would play, right? I mean, this is an unbelievable opportunity. I got boys, school team, coaches blowing up my DMs, blowing up my mentions by email, saying, our guys are saw your challenge. They can't wait to play."

It's one thing to stay radio silent on $10 million, but $100 million? That's 1/3 of the total estimated value of the Aces organization. It's three times their estimated annual revenue. How could they pass up that opportunity?

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

They would. Because it's not about the money. It's about knowing that the outcome is predetermined. Of course, an elite high school boys' basketball team would beat the WNBA champions, because they are bigger, faster and stronger than even the best women's basketball players. That doesn't mean the Aces' roster isn't full of extremely talented athletes in its own right or that the WNBA isn't worth watching or following. It's simply an acknowledgment of biological reality.

But denying that reality in favor of left-wing politics is a core tenet of the modern Democratic Party. And as such, the WNBA, the Aces and so on. That's why Travis was right to make the offer and about his motivations for doing so. The way to fight absurdity is with absurdity.

item.title: Pete Buttigieg distances himself from Biden amid 2028 talk, suggests 'Build Back Better' doesn't work
item.description: Pete Buttigieg distanced himself from former President Joe Biden's "Build Back Better" message and rejected a "return to normal" strategy amid 2028 rumors.
item.content:encoded:
Former Transportation Secretary and potential 2028 presidential candidate Pete Buttigieg appeared to distance himself from former President Joe Biden and rejected the idea of a "return to normal" during a Politico interview Tuesday.

"I'm trying to purge my vocabulary of anything with the prefix 're-' in it, anything with the word back in it," Buttigieg told columnist Jonathan Martin. "I don't think now is the time to be talking about 'Build Back Better.' Build better, yes. I don't even want to talk about back."

Martin pointed out that "Build Back Better" was Biden's 2020 presidential campaign slogan and asked if that meant he believed the party has changed in the last six years.

JAMES CARVILLE ARGUES ONE KEY MISTAKE FROM BIDEN HAS LEFT DEMOCRATS IN DISARRAY

"Yeah, I mean, I think, you know, if that could have worked, it would have worked," Buttigieg said.

Overall, Buttigieg rejected the idea of pushing a "return to normal" message that was the staple of Biden's original campaign.

"But to me, the most important thing is — are we demonstrating a readiness to be focused on building what’s next or are we basically preaching some version of 'return to normal'? 'Return to normal,' in my view, won’t work."

"One way to say I’m not a 'return to normal' is to present the idea that looks furthest left, because that makes you, in a certain way, seem bold. I don’t think it’s the only way to be bold. And so, I think it is really important to not let it lapse into a 'left versus center' thing, when the most important question to me is, are we going to try to sell some version of a previous status quo?" Buttigieg said.

BUTTIGIEG REVEALS HOW HE'D ADVISE DEMOCRATS ON KEY ISSUES IF HE COULD TIME TRAVEL BACK TO 2020

The former Biden official also "couldn't say" the former president was a mentor to him, though he referred to him as a "good man" and a "good boss."

"I wasn't close enough to him to say that," Buttigieg said. "But I would say that he, again, after I competed against him, and he beat me and everybody else in that primary, he gave me a tremendous opportunity to do a lot of work that I cared about, that was meaningful, that I'm proud of ... I learned a lot from him, but I wouldn't say I was close enough to him that I claim that."

Fox News Digital reached out to Biden's office for comment but did not immediately receive a response. 

Buttigieg's comments came after a University of New Hampshire Granite State Poll published last month showed him neck-and-neck with Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-N.Y., in a potential 2028 match-up, though he has yet to fully commit to another presidential run.

KAMALA HARRIS LEAVES BIDEN OFF LIST OF TOP THREE 'MOST EFFECTIVE' PRESIDENTS

In light of this, Buttigieg has doubled down on far-left proposals such as eliminating the Electoral College or expanding the Supreme Court while downplaying concerns over the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) and its candidates.

"I think one of the reasons why you see people who run on a promise of shaking it up, whether it's a DSA candidate on the left or whether it’s someone like Donald Trump, is because people can tell that the system we have is not just showing its age — it's letting us down," Buttigieg said on "America Reports."

The comment drew criticism from Fox News political analyst Reince Priebus, who served as RNC chairman and White House chief of staff to President Donald Trump in his first term, warning that Democrats like Buttigieg are aligning with people on "the wrong side of normal."

"The opponent — the Democrats from where Pete Buttigieg is at — is aligning itself with people that are far outside the mainstream. They're on the wrong side of normal, and he didn't really address that when he was pressed," Priebus said on "America Reports." "And that's the big question for him."

item.title: Dems in the hot seat for skipping crucial hearing on radical group hiding in US: 'Embarrassment'
item.description: Every Democratic Party member of a Senate Judiciary subcommittee boycotted a hearing on the Muslim Brotherhood's alleged U.S. network, describing the hearing as "a political creepshow."
item.content:encoded:
Democratic lawmakers were missing during Wednesday's Senate Judiciary subcommittee hearing, skipping a hearing on the Muslim Brotherhood’s alleged network inside the United States and drawing a blistering rebuke from Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas.

"You may notice that there are empty chairs on the Democrat side of the dais," Cruz said as he opened the hearing by pointing out every Democratic member of the subcommittee refused to attend. "The American people should ask themselves why not a single member of the minority decided that a hearing on terrorism was worth their time? It is an embarrassment."

Cruz tied the Democrats’ boycott to Abdul El-Sayed’s primary victory, arguing the timing helped explain why no Democratic members attended. Cruz accused the party of embracing a candidate who had campaigned alongside left-wing streamer Hasan Piker. 

Cruz cited Piker’s past statement that "America deserved 9/11" and asked the witnesses what El-Sayed’s rise said about the direction of the Democratic Party.

HASAN PIKER UNLOADS ON 'ISLAMOPHOBIC PIECES OF S---' DEMOCRATS AS EL-SAYED FACES PARTY UNITY TEST

"Abdul El-Sayed, the son-in-law of a leading member of several Brotherhood groups, won Michigan’s Democrat primary for U.S. Senate. Perfect timing for this hearing. Probably explains why no Democrats are here, and none intend to attend," Cruz said. 

"Because their campaign is now openly embracing terrorist organizations waging war on America."

The five Democratic members of the subcommittee — senators Sheldon Whitehouse of Rhode Island, Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut, Mazie Hirono of Hawaii, Alex Padilla of California and Peter Welch of Vermont — announced beforehand that they would not attend. In a joint statement, the senators accused Cruz of staging a "political creepshow" that scapegoated Muslim Americans.

"Scapegoating Muslims may be a Texas Republican strategist’s idea of ‘solid gold’ to whip up their voters, but Democrats have no intention of indulging this political creepshow, particularly after the recent violence targeting places of faith," they said. "Our focus is the costs families face thanks to rampant, non-stop Trump corruption."

Blumenthal separately told reporters Wednesday that Democrats refused to attend because the hearing "could well be used as an anti-Muslim, Islamophobia kind of show trial."

MICHIGAN SENATE RACE: EL-SAYED’S TIES TO EXTREMIST FUEL ANTISEMITISM CONCERNS AMONG JEWISH VOTERS

The Connecticut Democrat added that he planned to meet with members of the Muslim community who shared concerns about the Muslim Brotherhood, "which appears to be a terrorist organization," while advocating for "tolerance and inclusion."

The offices of Whitehouse and Welch referred Fox News Digital to the joint statement when asked why the senators chose to boycott rather than attend and challenge the witnesses directly. The offices of Hirono and Padilla had not responded by publication time.

Cruz and the hearing’s witnesses rejected the Democrats’ characterization of the proceeding as an attack on Muslims generally.

Lara Burns, a retired FBI special agent who helped lead a terrorism-financing investigation into what was once the largest Muslim charity in the United States, the Holy Land Foundation, warned that Americans should not disregard evidence because it is politically controversial.

"For decades, narratives have been intentionally seeded into public discourse that portray terrorist organizations as resistance movements," Burns testified before arguing Americans cannot "ignore evidence introduced in federal court simply because that evidence is politically uncomfortable."

"The history of this network is not in question," she added. "It was made public decades ago, but few paid attention. Now is the time to pay attention and understand the facts."

item.title: The Left wants Caitlin Clark, Sophie Cunningham to shut up and dribble when it comes to trans sports
item.description: Liberal sports media now wants Caitlin Clark to shut up and dribble on transgender athletes after demanding she speak on cultural issues for years.
item.content:encoded:
All of a sudden, it is liberal members of the sports media who want athletes like Caitlin Clark and Sophie Cunningham to stick to sports.

"Caitlin Clark just wants to shut up and dribble, and it's time we respect that," far-left sportswriter Dan Wolken wrote in a Yahoo column this week.

The column is in reference to Clark declining to comment on Cunningham's recent remarks about wanting to keep biological males out of female athletics.

"I think for us, it's not really a discussion we have in our locker room," Clark said when asked about Cunningham's comments. "I think that's for leagues and governing bodies to work with their athletes to find solutions, but our focus is on basketball. That's what we talk about and how we can get wins, and obviously we didn't do that tonight."

On the surface, we agree with the left's newfound stance on Caitlin Clark.

Clark does not owe anyone a comment on transgender participation in sports or any other issue unrelated to basketball. She has spent her entire life preparing to become a professional basketball player. She has no obligation to become the public face of any cultural issue.

The problem is that many of the very people suddenly insisting Clark should be left alone spent the past three seasons refusing to leave her alone.

ELLE DUNCAN BLAMES CAITLIN CLARK, HER FANS FOR MEDIA SMEAR CAMPAIGN WHILE IGNORING FACTS

The same commentators now criticizing conservatives for asking Clark about transgender athletes repeatedly demanded that she address what they described as the racism and homophobia directed at the WNBA's Black and lesbian players following her arrival in the league.

Just last week, former ESPN host Elle Duncan called for Clark to do exactly that.

"I would love for it to be very clear to the people who think they are her fans but are using her, if she would say, 'Stop that s---. I don't want it. I'm tired of it,'" Duncan said on The Sports Gossip Show podcast. "As opposed to what we've seen, which is, 'The media makes up these narratives. The media makes up this discourse.'"

Hill, David Dennis Jr., Cari Champion, Ros Gold-Onwude, Dan Le Batard and countless others made similar demands. They wanted Clark to legitimize their manufactured crisis.

Notice that Wolken never argued the media should respect Clark's then.

Now, they all want her to shut up and dribble.

DAN LE BATARD CLAIMS ESPN IS RUN BY MCAFEE AND 'WHITE PEOPLE' AFTER LAYOFFS, SLANDERS OUTKICK IN UNHINGED RANT

Next, let's try to have the type of conversation that few have managed to have about Caitlin Clark. A nuanced one.

The conservatives involved in this debate do not come away looking particularly strong either. It's fair to ask Clark about transgender athletes, given the attention the issue has received over the past week. However, calling her a "coward" for declining to answer reeks of the same entitlement conservatives often accuse the left of displaying.

"Caitlin Clark might be the biggest coward in the history of sports," Daily Wire commentator Matt Walsh said. "She refuses to say anything about the anti-white racism she has been subjected to since coming into the league. She punts on the trans question, which is the easiest question you could ever be asked. No spine."

Meanwhile, Awful Announcing is enjoying the spectacle, gloating that "Conservative media ate Caitlin Clark up. Now they're spitting her out."

We understand why some people believe Clark should simply say that biological males should not compete in women's sports. For one, that position is hardly fringe. According to Pew Research, roughly 78% of Americans agree. That includes Democrats, Republicans, and independents.

The WNBA exists because sports are separated by sex. There would be no WNBA if men's and women's athletics were not separate. Howard Bryant's comparison this week between Cunningham's comments and Colin Kaepernick's protests was both ignorant and desperate.

Still, the topic of transgender athletes has become deeply divisive in American politics. Therefore, it is entirely understandable that Clark would rather stay out of it entirely.

Cunningham is not a villain for sharing that view. Clark is also not a coward for declining to discuss it. Both statements can be true at once.

As has so often been the case throughout her WNBA career, Caitlin Clark once again looks like the only adult in the room.

While everyone around her manufactures outrage, she continues to handle herself like a professional.

Amid the toxic discourse, Clark has put together one of the greatest seven-game stretches in WNBA history, averaging 26.1 points and 8.6 assists per game.

Caitlin Clark is one of the few star athletes in America today who just wants to play ball. No amount of political pressure will change that.

As hard as it is for some to fathom, Caitlin Clark isn't interested in the culture war. She just wants to play basketball.

Let her.

item.title: Former Disney star Bella Thorne says cruel accusations after nude photo blackmail attempt 'really broke me'
item.description: Bella Thorne revealed on "Call Her Daddy" how the FBI traced her alleged hacker's identity through the screenshots she posted on social media.
item.content:encoded:
Bella Thorne fought back against an alleged blackmailer by releasing her own nude photos in 2019. But the former Disney star said it was the flood of victim-blaming accusations that "really, really broke" her.

The former Disney Channel star found herself at the center of a headline-making scandal when she accused a hacker of attempting to blackmail her with private nude photos. Thorne ultimately beat the alleged extortionist to the punch by releasing the images herself.

"I just did an honest Twitter post," Thorne recalled during an appearance on "Call Her Daddy." "I just kind of set it out as ... you're not gonna keep taking this from me, so here it is."

Thorne said she shared the images to take control of the situation before the alleged blackmailer could release them. The decision sparked a wave of backlash that the "Shake It Up" star said left her emotionally devastated.

"And you know, I think the worst part of that was people saying, 'Well, you did this. You are faking it. You just wanna show us your t---. You want us so badly to see your private parts that that's why you're doing it. You want it.' And that, to me, like, really broke me then. That like, really, really broke me," Thorne told host Alexandra Cooper.

The 28-year-old actress recalled filming an Instagram story in which she was "completely ... broken and so upset, just mad."

item.title: Ride malfunctions at popular Jersey Shore boardwalk, leaving riders hanging upside down
item.description: Video captures passengers trapped upside down on the Wipe Out ride at Ocean City Boardwalk after an apparent malfunction halted the attraction mid-cycle.
item.content:encoded:
Visitors looking for thrills at a popular boardwalk got more than they bargained for after a ride unexpectedly ground to a halt, forcing passengers to wait in a situation few would want to find themselves in.

Video shared on Instagram appears to show the Wipe Out ride at the Ocean City Boardwalk stopped mid-cycle with riders suspended upside down as concerned spectators gathered below.

In the clip, women can be heard yelling as one bystander tries to reassure those trapped on the ride.

EIGHT RIDERS LEFT DANGLING ATOP 100-FOOT ROLLER COASTER FOR OVER THREE HOURS AT TEXAS AMUSEMENT PARK

"You're alright honey! You're alright!" one person can be heard shouting.

The video quickly sparked a wave of reactions on social media, with many viewers expressing relief that the ride's safety restraints appeared to do their job despite the frightening ordeal.

"On a positive note: whoever designed the safety harnesses should get a MASSIVE raise," one Instagram user wrote.

SIX FLAGS GUESTS STRANDED 245 FEET IN AIR AFTER POWER OUTAGE FORCES COASTER EVACUATION

Others said the incident reminded them of similar experiences.

"My cousins were stuck on a ride in Ocean City 20 years ago. Still happening," another commenter wrote.

Some viewers tried to lighten the mood, with one writing, "You are in fact not alright honey, you're upside down for way longer than you should be."

It was not immediately clear what caused the apparent malfunction, how long riders remained suspended, or whether anyone was injured.

Fox News Digital has reached out to the Ocean City Fire Department, Ocean City Police Department, the ride's operator and the New Jersey Department of Community Affairs for comment.

item.title: Miranda Kerr's ultra-specific diet includes venison for breakfast, no eggs or seed oils
item.description: Miranda Kerr revealed her strict diet, including venison for breakfast, no eggs and zero seed oils or dairy. She said eating better has helped her feel better.
item.content:encoded:
Miranda Kerr recently detailed her ultra healthy, if a bit unique, diet, which includes eating venison for breakfast and cutting out eggs altogether.

"I love food, but when I got sick, I had to learn even more that food is medicine," the former Victoria’s Secret Angel told Kristin Cavallari on her "Let’s be Honest" podcast. "So, I love to have nutritious and delicious foods that feed my soul, but, at the same time, I don’t crave like unhealthy food anymore because I know how detrimental that can be to my body on the inside, not even about what it looks like on the outside, but on the inside.

"I want to have vitality and energy and that’s kind of why I eat healthy."

Two years ago, Kerr revealed she was diagnosed with proctitis, a form of irritable bowl syndrome, when she was pregnant with her second son six years earlier.

MIRANDA KERR RECALLS FIRST MEETING EX ORLANDO BLOOM'S FIANCEE KATY PERRY: 'WE JUST IMMEDIATELY GOT ALONG'

She told Get the Gloss at the time she drank a liter of celery juice a day, which is known to be an anti-inflammatory, and said she is now in remission.

The 43-year-old supermodel told Cavallari she wants to be able to run around with her grandkids someday, "be baking them cakes like my grandma did for me" and feel healthy "for as long as" she can.

"‘Cause I think that’s more important than what you look like," she argued. "It’s so much more important that you feel that vitality, and that’s why I say that my non-negotiables are meditation. Like, I’m doing that instead of working out, I guess you could say, with the busy life that I have right now, but that’s the choice that I make because that’s what feeds me."

She said other people might be "really fed" by going for a run in the morning, for example. 

"Each to their own. You have to find what elevates you, what de-stresses you," she said. 

She also loves dance parties with her kids.

Kerr shares Flynn, 15, with ex-husband Orlando Bloom and Hart, 8, Myles, 6, and Pierre, 2, with her husband, Snapchat founder Evan Spiegel.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

She said she’s been drinking Noni juice, which she calls a "superfood superfruit," in the morning for 30 years since she was 13.

"What I love about it is it’s full of antioxidants, and it has a lot of vitamins and minerals."

She said she drinks a 30-millimeter shot, and her youngest child has some as well, but she admitted her teenager is "not into it."

Kerr then has a marshmallow tea "because that’s good for the gut lining. S,o I get the marshmallow leaf, and then I put it and brew it in hot water."

That's followed by a few tablespoons of coconut yogurt with honey and a bite of a banana.

"I do all of this before I have my coffee. I get to my coffee, and my coffee is my moment where I’m in bliss," she admitted.

Her Fabula brand coffee, which she said is mold- and lead-free, includes coconut milk from high-end grocery store Erewhon and maple syrup.

She also doesn’t eat eggs.

"I do proteins, like meats like venison, bison, lamb, turkey. I eat all the meats that aren’t mass-produced for the reasons that we all know," she explained. 

MIRANDA KERR'S HUSBAND, EVAN SPIEGEL, PRAISES HER 'VERY DIFFERENT' CO-PARENTING RELATIONSHIP WITH ORLANDO BLOOM

"I’m not much of a fruit girl, to be honest, but I will have a banana, and I also think a banana is a great snack to go," she said. "I do love mangoes."

She also stays away from dairy and wheat, "and I’m very specific about the oils, so only cooking with coconut oil or avocado oil. No seed oils."

Kerr said she does tallow sometimes, "mostly for the kids." She also tries to get them to eat sourdough because they refuse to eat gluten-free bread.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Lots of squash, carrots and parsnips are also on the menu. 

"And I do have a little bit of salmon but not too much because of the mercury that’s in salmon," she said.

The model said she used to "live on sushi" when she lived in New York, but she doesn't eat it anymore because of the possibility of parasites.

"I do love caviar," she admitted. "Caviar’s good. There’s no parasites there."

As far as sweets, she likes carob, and she and her younger kids have tea parties where they drink lemon balm tea with carob.

"I do like chocolate, and, so, I also will make, like, a carob hot chocolate with coconut milk, maple syrup, carob. It’s really good," she added.

item.title: Search for Amelia Earhart's long-lost plane reignites with ambitious new expedition
item.description: The Taraia Object Expedition departs on Oct. 7 for Nikumaroro Island to investigate a satellite-imaged anomaly believed to be Amelia Earhart's long-missing plane.
item.content:encoded:
Researchers are gearing up to resume their search for Amelia Earhart's lost plane in the Pacific Ocean after setbacks delayed the search.

Purdue University officials said in a recent statement that researchers will travel to Nikumaroro Island in the Pacific to investigate the Taraia Object, a satellite-imaged anomaly believed by some to be Earhart's lost Lockheed Electra.

The expedition, called the Taraia Object Expedition, will depart on Oct. 7.

AMELIA EARHART MYSTERY EXPEDITION HALTED AS RESEARCHERS SEEK ANSWERS ON MISSING PLANE

"The expedition seeks to help complete the historic journey that ended with her disappearance 89 years ago," officials said. 

The expedition is based on researchers' belief that Earhart's plane came down near Nikumaroro, known as the Nikumaroro Hypothesis.

Supporters of the theory believe that Earhart and navigator Fred Noonan became stranded on the remote island after failing to reach Howland Island — possibly dying as castaways.

Earhart disappeared on July 2, 1937, while attempting to become the first female pilot to fly around the world.

NEWLY RELEASED AMELIA EARHART DOCUMENTS REVEAL VIVID DETAILS OF JAPAN'S ROLE IN SEARCH FOR DOOMED AVIATOR

She and Noonan lost contact during one of the final legs of their journey, going missing after leaving Lae, New Guinea, en route to Howland Island.

She was 39 years old at the time and one of the most famous people in the world.

The upcoming expedition was announced last year but was delayed while officials awaited approval from the government of Kiribati. The country's cabinet has since approved the mission.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Richard Pettigrew, founder and executive director of the Archaeological Legacy Institute, which is leading the expedition, said that he is "grateful for the patience and enthusiasm of everyone who has followed this journey with us."

"The evidence supporting the Nikumaroro Hypothesis remains compelling, and the only way to answer this question is to go to Nikumaroro, inspect the Taraia Object firsthand and follow the evidence wherever it leads," Pettigrew said in a statement.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

Fox News Digital reached out to Purdue University for comment.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The story of Earhart's disappearance has captivated Americans for decades and has been the subject of ongoing research.

Last year, the National Archives released over 4,600 pages of previously unsealed government records related to Earhart's 1937 disappearance, including her final known radio transmissions.

More recently, pilot Justin Myers said he identified a possible image of Earhart's missing Lockheed Electra in Google Earth imagery of Nikumaroro.

item.title: Spokane fire survivor finds 'joy' through Jesus after alleged arson destroys home and belongings
item.description: Christopher Guyton says losing his home in the Spokane wildfire strengthened his Christian faith and inspired him to spread the Gospel to others.
item.content:encoded:
Spokane wildfire survivor Christopher Guyton said losing his home to one of Washington state’s most devastating wildfires strengthened his faith and inspired him to spread the Gospel.

Guyton shared his faithful message Wednesday on "America Reports" as fire survivors across the Spokane area look to rebuild their lives after three separate fires reportedly burned over 10,000 acres and destroyed more than 700 structures.

"I'm able to see very clearly the love of Jesus Christ," Guyton said. "There are a lot of people out there that lost their homes that don't have Jesus, and that is way worse... what this makes me want to do is go spread the Gospel."

SPENCER PRATT REACTS TO SPOKANE DEVASTATION WITH BLUNT WILDFIRE WARNING AND MESSAGE OF FAITH

Flames tore through the Spokane area over the weekend, leaving neighborhoods with charred vehicles, melted plastic recycling bins and ash-covered lots that were once homes.

Guyton, an audio designer who moved to Spokane in 2020, lamented how his family and so many others lost "everything" in the "blink of an eye."

The Spokane resident lost cherished personal belongings, including his music studio and retro video game collection, though his wife, two children and cat escaped unharmed.

"My 3-year-old, she doesn't really understand why we can't go home," he told Fox News. "My 1-year-old is a little bit too young to really understand anything.

"We haven't showed them any of this just because we feel like it would just be too traumatic for them."

Guyton expressed gratitude for the support of his church community as he and his family look to rebuild their lives.

"It's been pretty difficult, but, luckily, we have a really supportive church family, and we are just super blessed with everything that we've been given to just try to start putting the pieces back together," Guyton said.

He said navigating the loss of a home has been easier because of his faith, explaining that the "joy" he finds in Christianity helps ease the pain.

VIRGIN MARY STATUE BECOMES BEACON OF HOPE AFTER CALIFORNIA WILDFIRES, FOX NATION EXPLORES

"[My pastor] always talks about the difference between joy and happiness," Guyton said. "He says, ‘Joy is something that you get from God, and when you have joy, you can still feel sadness, but there's a lightness to that sadness.’"

The grief that comes with such a devastating loss, Guyton said, feels more manageable because of his relationship with God, adding that he hopes to use his devastation to introduce more people to Jesus’ love.

"When you're depressed, sadness is really heavy, and happiness is really, really heavy as well. But we have joy because we have Jesus," Guyton said.

Aaron Farinacci, 37, was charged with first-degree arson after being accused of intentionally setting the Old Trails Fire, the largest of the three Spokane blazes. Officials say Farinacci was questioned by police about two other wildfires in 2025.

Guyton said Farinacci’s alleged arson is a "real shame" and only makes the tragedy "worse" as the family of four grapples with how to move forward without their home.

"I hope that all the authorities that are involved in this can find some way to make this right with everyone," he concluded.

item.title: Brewery behind Trump, McConnell death promotions now unveils 'Antifa Octoberfist' beer
item.description: Minocqua Brewing Company released its "Antifa Octoberfist" beer after Abdul El-Sayed won Michigan's Democratic primary for a Senate nomination.
item.content:encoded:
The Wisconsin brewery that previously drew national attention for promising free beer "the day" President Donald Trump dies and later announcing plans for a "half-price beer day" when Sen. Mitch McConnell dies is again courting controversy with the release of a politically themed beer called "Antifa Octoberfist."

In a Wednesday social media post, Minocqua Brewing Company said it chose to announce the seasonal beer after "another card-carrying member of ANTIFA" won a Democratic primary in Michigan.

The brewery said the beer's label revisits the question, "Is it OK to punch a Nazi?" and references Captain America and World War II while promoting the product.

REPUBLICANS GET THE DEMOCRAT THEY WANTED AS SOCIALIST ABDUL EL-SAYED WINS MICHIGAN SENATE PRIMARY

"Now that another card-carrying member of ANTIFA has won the Democratic Primary in Michigan, we thought today would be a good day to announce that our seasonal Octoberfest is BACK--and it's call ‘Antifa Octoberfist!’" the post read.

On Tuesday, Abdul El-Sayed defeated Rep. Haley Stevens, D-Mich., winning the Democratic nomination for Senate.

The brewery then shared the message printed on the back of the cans about punching Nazis.

"During World War II, America rose up against Nazi Germany and rejected the idea of fascism, which is defined as government lead by a strong man that fetishizes power, uses violence to quash opposition, demands absolute loyalty, and gains power by seducing those who perceive themselves as victims," the message reads.

WISCONSIN BREWERY THAT PROMISED FREE BEER WHEN TRUMP DIES NOW PLANS 'HALF-PRICE BEER DAY' WHEN MCCONNELL DIES

"Over the last 70 years, we’ve honored our American forefathers who vanquished fascism in Germany," it continued. "Those heroes were antifascists, or for short, ‘antifa.’ Unfortunately, fascism has once again reared its ugly head — not in Germany, but here at home, within America’s borders. That’s why we made Antifa OktoberFIST: a German-style Festbier that is uniquely American."

"Of course it’s not OK to punch anyone, but it’s patriotic as hell to raise your fist against fascism, reject its four tenets, and embrace the true American ideals of democracy, freedom, justice, and equality of opportunity."

The brewery previously sparked outrage by promising free beer on "the day" Trump dies in January, and again following the April shooting at the White House Correspondents’ Dinner. On Monday, it announced plans for a "half-price beer day" for when McConnell dies.

Minocqua Brewing Company is currently fighting getting their permit revoked.

The Milwaukee Journal Sentinel reported on July 27 that Wisconsin's Department of Revenue sent a notice to liberal activist and brewery owner Kirk Bangstad announcing plans to revoke the brewery’s permit.

WORLD-FAMOUS CATHOLIC SHRINE TORCHED, 'DEVIL IN A SKIRT' SCRAWLED ON VIRGIN MARY STATUE

The Sentinel reported that state regulators pursued revoking Bangstad's alcohol license after authorities seized canned beer from his company in June, alleging it had been transported from Illinois without the required permits and taxes. The paper also reported that Bangstad criticized the proposed action as an excessive response, arguing the alleged tax violations did not warrant shutting down his business.

The revocation of the beer permit was set to go into effect on Tuesday, but a spokesperson for Wisconsin's Department of Revenue told Fox News Digital in a statement Monday that "Minocqua Brewing Company has filed an administrative appeal, and, therefore, the permit will not be revoked, pending the outcome of the administrative appeal."

Fox News Digital reached out to Minocqua Brewing Company and El-Sayed for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

item.title: Russia deploys North Korean missile unit to Ukraine; Moscow-Pyongyang axis deepens: report
item.description: A Ukrainian intelligence official says Russia is deploying a North Korean unit with up to 120 ballistic missiles in its war against Ukraine.
item.content:encoded:
Russia has begun deploying a North Korean missile unit equipped with up to 120 ballistic missiles and six launchers for use in its war against Ukraine, a Ukrainian intelligence official told told Reuters Wednesday.

The reported escalation marks a deepening military partnership between Moscow and Pyongyang, with around 90 North Korean personnel expected to be stationed in Russia's western Voronezh region to support the new unit, according to Andrii Cherniak of Ukraine's Main Directorate of Intelligence (HUR).

Cherniak also claimed Pyongyang has already delivered a fresh batch of 40 KN-23 and KN-24 ballistic missiles to Russian forces, Reuters said.

RUSSIA LAUNCHES BALLISTIC MISSILE ATTACK ON KYIV HOURS AFTER ZELENSKYY WARNS OF MAJOR STRIKE

Final details of the deployment are expected to be finalized during high-level talks next month.

The intelligence report follows a massive Russian barrage against Kyiv and the surrounding region Aug. 4. 

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Moscow launched 24 ballistic missiles, four cruise missiles and 115 drones overnight, killing at least 17 people.

Zelenskyy argued more lives could have been saved had Western allies replenished Ukraine's depleted stockpiles of air defense interceptors.

Zelenskyy previously warned that Moscow had been preparing since June to receive additional North Korean military personnel in the Voronezh region, according to reports.

RUSSIA UNLEASHES NEARLY 600 MISSILES AND DRONES ON KYIV IN DEADLIEST STRIKE SINCE MAY

Cherniak told Reuters a Russian strike in late July marked the first recorded use of North Korean ballistic missiles against Ukrainian targets since August 2025.

According to HUR estimates, Russia has received approximately 150 KN-23 and KN-24 missiles from North Korea since late 2023.

Military analysts say Russia is increasingly relying on ballistic weapons because they require advanced defense systems — such as the U.S.-made Patriot — to intercept.

The Washington-based Institute for the Study of War (ISW) assessed that Russia is deliberately incorporating more ballistic missiles into its long-range strike packages to maximize pressure on Ukraine's limited air defenses.

ISW added that North Korea is gaining critical battlefield data from the conflict, allowing Pyongyang to refine its missile performance using Russian operational experience.

ALARMING MISSILE REPORT DRAWS FORCEFUL RESPONSE FROM TRUMP AS IRAN WAR TESTS AMERICA’S ARSENAL

North Korea has emerged as one of Moscow's key military allies since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine began.

Reuters reported that Pyongyang has supplied millions of artillery shells and previously sent 14,000 troops to Russia's Kursk region to counter Ukraine's 2024 cross-border incursion.

Cherniak also noted that roughly 9,500 North Korean troops are still in Kursk, though they are not engaged in active combat right now.

A report by the Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD) states that, since Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine, North Korea has supplied Moscow with large quantities of artillery and rocket ammunition, cannon and rocket artillery systems and ballistic missiles.

The policy institute described the Russia-North Korea relationship as one of the "most consequential among the Axis" and the only partnership in which one member has deployed troops in combat to assist another.

item.title: Three teams ranked outside the top-12 of the Coaches Poll who will make the College Football Playoff
item.description: Three teams ranked outside the top-12 in the coaches poll are poised for college football playoff berths, including LSU Tigers and SMU Mustangs.
item.content:encoded:
There are certain indicators that the college football season is right around the corner, and one of the biggest telltale signs is the release of the preseason polls.

Earlier this week, the USA Today Coaches Poll dropped and had plenty of fans arguing online about the rankings of certain teams as well as the merits of preseason polls in general.

While I don't have much of an issue with how the rankings came out, outside of a few spots here and there, I would like to identify a few teams that I believe will outperform their preseason ranking.

ONE OF THESE EIGHT COLLEGE FOOTBALL TEAMS WILL BE HOISTING THE NATIONAL CHAMPIONSHIP TROPHY IN 2026

To be clear, the Coaches Poll isn't the same as the College Football Playoff Rankings, but the top-12 of the preseason polls in a given year is generally indicative of who everyone thinks will be in the big dance come December.

With that in mind, here are three teams from outside the top-12 that will make the College Football Playoff in 2026.

Maybe I'm just drinking the Lane Kiffin-laced Kool-Aid, but I have a hard time seeing the LSU Tigers missing the CFP in 2026 given everything we know about them.

The hiring of Kiffin alone turned the Bayou Bengals into Playoff contenders almost overnight, but it goes beyond just the head coach.

WHAT DOES A REALISTICALLY SUCCESSFUL FIRST YEAR LOOK LIKE FOR HEAD COACH LANE KIFFIN AT LSU?

Both coordinators are considered some of the best in college, with offensive coordinator Charlie Weis Jr. and defensive coordinator Blake Baker likely headlining preseason Broyles Award watchlists.

When you pair that coaching triumvirate with the reported $40 million roster that's been put in place, which includes the nation's top-ranked transfer portal class, you start to realize LSU is working with some serious firepower.

I think 13 is a little low for this iteration of the Tigers, but I also doubt they'll be sneaking up on anyone.

Despite his public pleas for patience, Kiffin understands the elevated expectations at LSU, and I believe a Playoff appearance in 2026 is in the cards.

It's also the bare minimum in terms of accomplishments he will need to achieve to keep the heat off his back in year one.

Just two seasons ago, the SMU Mustangs shocked the college football world by making the Playoff in their first year in the ACC.

The Ponies took a step back in 2025 in terms of record, but when you peel the layers back, you realize how close they were to repeating as ACC representatives in the CFP.

That includes a double-overtime loss to Baylor in week two, and their only two losses in conference play came by a combined five points.

SMU HEAD COACH RHETT LASHLEE POURS GASOLINE ON FIRE, DISPARAGES SUN BELT'S CLAIM TO CFP BERTH

SMU ranks inside the top-25 in terms of returning production, and a big chunk of that comes in the form of veteran signal caller Kevin Jennings.

The redshirt senior comes back to Dallas with a ton of experience and even has a Playoff appearance of his own under his belt.

Both coordinators return as well, and the conference slate shapes up nicely, as the Mustangs avoid both Miami and Clemson in the regular season.

I could see SMU making a return trip to the ACC Championship Game in 2026, likely against the aforementioned Hurricanes.

Although the Canes look like the class of the conference on paper, the Mustangs defeated Miami as the less talented team just a season ago, and I trust head coach Rhett Lashlee in a one-game scenario as much as anyone in the ACC.

I wrote about these very same Houston Cougars about a month and a half ago, tabbing them as my dark horse pick to win the Big 12, so I decided to put my money where my mouth is and double down on them as CFP contenders.

Houston is 17th in the nation (and 2nd in the Big 12) in returning production overall, and top-ten when it comes to returning production on offense.

The Cougars added a lightning bug in running back Makhi Hughes from the transfer portal, and while he wasn't super productive while at Oregon, his numbers from his previous stop at Tulane were eye-popping, and he should have similar production in Texas.

I'm particularly impressed with young up-and-coming defensive coordinator Austin Armstrong, whose simulated pressure stylings have caused offenses headaches in recent years.

I believe the veteran experience on both sides of the ball plus a manageable Big 12 schedule will make the Cougs a tantalizing pick to win the conference.

In addition to avoiding BYU and both Arizona teams, Houston will get Texas Tech early.

The Red Raiders have been picked to win the conference by pretty much every writer with a pulse, but the Brendan Sorsby situation may have their quarterback room in flux.

It's better to get them early before their talent has a chance to gel, and if the Cougars get the drop on Texas Tech, they could have an inside path at winning the conference outright.

item.title: Abdul El-Sayed’s Medicare-for-all crusade collides with an awkward contradiction involving his wife
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed pushes Medicare-for-all, but his wife's psychiatry practice refuses all insurance, forcing patients to pay entirely out of pocket.
item.content:encoded:
Michigan Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed has campaigned on passing Medicare-for-all, but his wife’s private psychiatry practice appears to operate outside the insurance system entirely.

El-Sayed, who secured the Democratic nomination for Senate on Wednesday, has argued that "healthcare shouldn't depend on who signs your paycheck" and demanded that taxpayers pay to "guarantee healthcare from cradle to grave" through Medicare-for-all. Despite this, his wife, Sarah Jukaku, states on her medical practice’s website that she is out of network with all insurance companies, generally requiring patients to pay the practice directly, though some may be eligible for out-of-network reimbursement.

Prior to July 2026, the FAQ section of Jukaku's website for her practice included the question "do you accept my insurance?" accompanied by the answer "no," according to The Washington Free Beacon. Her profile on Psychology Today, a popular professional database for therapists and psychiatrists, also at one point noted that she did not accept insurance.

Jukaku operates her own practice where she is the sole physician.

DR MARC SIEGEL: A SENATE CANDIDATE'S MEDICAL TITLE SPARKS A DEBATE VOTERS SHOULDN'T IGNORE

Amid media scrutiny in July, the practice’s website became inaccessible to the public and displayed a message indicating that it was private. Fox News Digital reached Jukaku and her practice multiple times via phone and email but received no response.

It is not rare for psychiatrists to turn away patients on Medicare. A 2022 analysis by KFF found that 40% of psychiatrists did not participate in Medicare, among the highest rate of any medical specialty.

Even as his wife's psychiatry practice reportedly operates on an out-of-network model, El-Sayed has repeatedly stressed the importance of expanding access to government-backed healthcare.

In a 2020 interview with the National Alliance on Mental Illness, for instance, he stated that "my wife's a psychiatrist, and we talk about the fact that a lot of folks don't do psychiatry because it's not as well recompensed as other practices simply because it's undervalued in the system." He went on to argue that the United States needs to build a "system" that "recognizes" the importance of treating "mental illness" due to the prevalence of "serious mental illness" and "death by suicide."

Years later, at a September 2025 campaign event, El-Sayed lamented that individuals with "serious mental illness" often "fall out of care" due to "transitions in health insurance."

MICHIGAN DEM SENATOR THROWS SUPPORT BEHIND CANDIDATE TO REPLACE HIM IN CONTENTIOUS PRIMARY

The couple reported nearly $686,000 in total income in 2025, underscoring the contrast between El-Sayed's calls for expanded government-backed healthcare and his wife's out-of-network psychiatry practice.

The couple reported $686,069 in total income and $675,246 in adjusted gross income on two pages of their 2025 tax return released Wednesday. El-Sayed also sports a collection of luxury watches ranging in value from $2,000 to $10,000 apiece.

MICHIGAN SENATE HOPEFUL ABDUL EL-SAYED FIRES BACK AT CNN CHOOSING TO 'FIXATE' ON 'DEFUND THE POLICE' COMMENTS

"He regularly wears a SAR Rescue Timer on the campaign trail because he is trying to rescue our politics from corporate corruption," El-Sayed spokeswoman Roxie Richner told The Washington Free Beacon. "Sometimes he wears a vintage doctor's watch because he is a doctor."

Though El-Sayed earned a medical degree, he was never a licensed physician, which caused controversy amid allegations that he had claimed to be a practicing doctor.

"He has earned the right to be called ‘doctor’ twice over," a campaign spokesperson said at the time, alluding to the fact that he received both a medical degree and a doctorate degree in public health.

The El-Sayed campaign and Jukaku did not respond to requests for comment when reached by Fox News Digital.

item.title: JD Vance warns 'limousine socialists' will destroy Michigan auto jobs, depress American wages
item.description: JD Vance labels Abdul El-Sayed a "limousine socialist," claiming the Michigan Senate candidate's policies on immigration and tariffs hurt auto workers.
item.content:encoded:
Vice President JD Vance branded Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed a "limousine socialist," on Wednesday, warning that the far-left is using wealth redistribution and open-border immigration to undermine Michigan's working-class autoworkers.

Speaking on "The Ingraham Angle," Vance argued that the victory of Democratic candidates backed by the far-left exposes a party pushing wealth redistribution rather than domestic industrial growth.

"They're not promising you industry. They're not promising you good jobs. They're not promising self-sufficiency in a good industrial economy. What they're promising is redistribution," Vance told host Laura Ingraham.

2026 MIDTERMS STATE OF PLAY: KEY RACES UNFOLD AS STEVENS, EL-SAYED BATTLE IN MICHIGAN

The vice president addressed the primary victory of El-Sayed in Michigan’s Democratic U.S. Senate race. El-Sayed, a progressive backed by figures like Sen. Bernie Sanders and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, narrowly defeated Rep. Haley Stevens and is now set to face Republican candidate Mike Rogers in November.

Vance said that primary victories for candidates further left of center reflect a broader shift in the party, arguing that the "base of the Democratic Party just wants radicals."

"It wants people who hate even the idea of private property ownership. But it also, I think, tells us that, that particular set of ideas is very popular in places you wouldn't expect because El-Sayed, he's this guy who holds himself out as a working-class hero, as a guy who's going to fight for the working class," Vance said.

"How does he fight for the working class? By flooding his state and his country with low-wage immigrants. Of course, those people will drive down the wages of the working class. And he also doesn't want to do anything to protect the Michigan auto industry. He has fought against the Trump tariffs that have saved the Michigan auto industry," he added.

TRUMP JUST EXPANDED HIS TARIFF PLAYBOOK WITH A POWERFUL TRADE WEAPON NO PRESIDENT HAS EVER USED

Fox News Digital reached out to the El-Sayed campaign for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

Vance continued by labeling El-Sayed as one of the "limousine socialists" he said are anti-industry. While Stevens focused her campaign on manufacturing and the state’s auto industry, El-Sayed ran on a more progressive platform, advocating for "Medicare-for-All" and campaign finance reform.

"We've seen this in Europe and in the United States. The idea that you can build real prosperity by just redistributing assets from one group to another group. That's not how you build real prosperity. You have to actually sustain the foundation of the economy," Vance said.

"That is what the President of the United States has worked us towards for the past 18 months. It's going to continue to pay dividends," he added.

TOP WISCONSIN DEMOCRATIC SOCIALIST CANDIDATE CONFRONTED ON PAST 'DEFUND POLICE' RHETORIC

Watch the full interview with Vice President Vance on "The Ingraham Angle" at 7 p.m. ET.

item.title: MLB player Adley Rutschman's Red Sox trade ruined 'Spider-Man' movie plans with Orioles teammates
item.description: Adley Rutschman and three Orioles teammates were headed to see "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" when the MLB trade deadline call changed everything.
item.content:encoded:
The big-league movie plans were over before they ever began.

Adley Rutschman, Colton Cowser, Ryan Mountcastle and Gunnar Henderson had plans to see "Spider-Man: Brand New Day."

Then Rutschman's phone rang.

It was the Baltimore Orioles' front office with trade deadline news: Rutschman had been dealt.

MLB TRADE DEADLINE DELIVERS BLOCKBUSTER MOVES FOR ADLEY RUTSCHMAN FREDDY PERALTA AND KEVIN GAUSMAN

Among Monday's flurry of MLB headlines, Rutschman's move to the Boston Red Sox stood out as one of the biggest. The former No. 1 overall pick and three-time All-Star had spent his entire major league career in Baltimore.

Boston landed Rutschman and catcher Jake Rogers, sending top pitching prospects Anthony Eyanson and Kyson Witherspoon, outfielder Enddy Azocar, catcher Carlos Narvaez and a player to be named later to Baltimore.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

A low-key afternoon with the boys quickly turned into an emotional goodbye for one of the Orioles' closest-knit groups. Speaking to the media a day later, Cowser described the ill-fated movie plans that turned into a trade deadline farewell.

"There was some shock there," Cowser recalled when describing the moment Rutschman received the news.

"You could kind of see it on his face that something might have been brewing up. I guess you could say there's a little bit of shock factor. It was pretty emotional yesterday. I think that the initial shock of it was something that was tough to see. Definitely some sadness there, and all I could do was give him a hug and tell him that I'm here for him and I love him. So yeah, it was obviously tough."

Cowser also reflected on what Rutschman meant to the clubhouse.

"He's an exceptional talent, can hit from both sides of the plate, exceptional on defense, and someone who's been anchoring this team for the past four-and-a-half years. He's truly going to be missed here. And as a friend, he's someone who's grown really close to me."

RED SOX FANS BEG TEAM TO TRADE 'TOXIC' JARREN DURAN AFTER YET ANOTHER EMBARRASSING INCIDENT

Rutschman, meanwhile, acknowledged the emotions of leaving the only organization he'd known while turning the page to Boston.

"Played my entire career there and been a lot of unbelievable memories, made a lot of great friends for life," Rutschman said, via MLB.com. "It's tough goodbyes, but we're onto the next thing and excited to be here and playing. It's all part of the game."

One minute, Rutschman was headed to see the friendly neighborhood web-slinger.

The next, he was headed to Boston, repping a brand-new team.

item.title: Trump's antitrust point man could reshape Big Tech cases against Google and Apple if confirmed
item.description: Adam Candeub's Senate confirmation hearing could reshape landmark antitrust cases against Google and Apple as he pushes for Section 230 reform.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump's pick to lead the Justice Department's Antitrust Division testified before the Senate on Wednesday in a confirmation hearing that could shape the future direction of the government's fight against Big Tech.

If confirmed, Adam Candeub, a longtime telecommunications law scholar and former Federal Communications Commission general counsel, would take control of some of the most consequential antitrust cases in decades, including the Justice Department’s landmark lawsuits targeting Google’s dominance in online search and Apple’s control over the App Store and its rules for developers.

The cases could determine how aggressively the government pursues antitrust cases against the country's largest technology companies.

FOX NEWS POLL: MOVE OVER BIG BROTHER, VOTERS SEE BIG TECH AS GREATER THREAT TO US

As head of the Antitrust Division, Candeub would oversee those cases and decide whether to continue the Justice Department's aggressive antitrust efforts against the largest technology companies.

Candeub has emerged as one of the conservative movement’s most prominent critics of Big Tech, arguing that dominant online platforms have accumulated too much power and that regulators have historically overlooked the larger impact of technology companies on competition, speech and public discourse.

"Big Tech’s market power undermines our nation’s culture of vibrant democratic deliberation," Candeub testified before Congress in March 2023. "Elon Musk’s Twitter files demonstrated that Big Tech has indeed limited particular groups, including dissenters, from important government policies from full participation in national political discussions.

"This power to exclude threatens all Americans," Candeub continued. "Power to silence one group of Americans will be used sooner or later to silence another."

META MEDICARE SCAM ADS TARGETING SENIORS FACE SCRUTINY

Candeub has pushed for changes to Section 230, the federal law that protects online platforms from being held liable for much of the content posted by users. During Trump's first administration, he served at the National Telecommunications and Information Administration, where he helped lead efforts to narrow those legal protections for online platforms under Section 230.

And in his contribution to Project 2025, the conservative policy blueprint developed by the Heritage Foundation for a potential second Trump administration, Candeub argued that antitrust enforcement failed to account for the influence of major technology platforms over competition and the flow of information being shared.

"The large internet platforms have transformed the U.S. economy, streamlining consumer purchases, networking billions of people, and altering long-established business practices," Candeub wrote. "Despite their enormous size, they have avoided significant antitrust liability or prosecution. The reasons for this are not entirely clear."

Candeub’s nomination has drawn support from former Justice Department officials, including former Attorney General Bill Barr, who appointed Candeub as an associate deputy attorney general in 2020 during the first Trump administration.

TODD BLANCHE 'HONORED AND HUMBLED' BY TRUMP'S AG NOMINATION AFTER EXPLOSIVE WEEK OF FEDERAL ARRESTS

Barr praised Candeub’s expertise in telecommunications law and his academic background, describing him as a knowledgeable and capable leader for the Antitrust Division.

"I think he'll be a strong leader, and he's very knowledgeable," Barr told Fox News Digital. "I think he'll be balanced and fair and apply the law."

Barr is among more than a dozen current and former Justice Department officials who signed a letter to the Senate Judiciary Committee supporting Candeub’s nomination. The letter highlighted his experience at the FCC, the Office of the Associate Attorney General, the NTIA and his work as a law professor at Michigan State University.

INDIANA REPUBLICAN SENATOR MOVES TO BLOCK KIDS FROM ACCESSING PORN ONLINE

"Adam Candeub has the experience and the qualifications to live up to that storied legacy," the letter stated, arguing that the Antitrust Division’s next leader must be prepared to address the growing challenges posed by technology, social media and artificial intelligence.

"The Division’s next leader must be able to meet those questions with both intellectual seriousness and practical judgment," the letter continued. "Mr. Candeub is uniquely qualified to do so."

Sen. Dick Durbin, D-Ill., said on X that he recently met with Candeub to discuss issues including merger reviews, Section 230 reform and efforts to protect children online.

item.title: Rita Wilson ignored her mother's old-school marriage advice, and it led her to Tom Hanks
item.description: Rita Wilson revealed on Michelle Obama's podcast the outdated marriage advice her mom gave before she found love with Tom Hanks on set in 1984.
item.content:encoded:
Rita Wilson is sharing the marriage advice her mom gave that didn't sit right with her.

During a recent appearance on Michelle Obama's podcast, "In My Opinion," the 69-year-old actress spoke about the outdated marriage advice her mom gave her before she met and married Tom Hanks.

"I was engaged before I got engaged to my husband. If I had married that person, I would have been divorced within a year," she said. "I thought that was what you were supposed to do at a certain age. I actually thought, because I had never really fallen in love with anyone, that I would be OK."

While engaged to that man, Wilson said she asked her mom for advice, telling her, "I don't know though. Should I marry him? I'm not really in love with him," and getting a surprising response in return.

'SHAMELESS' STAR EMMY ROSSUM REVEALS SECRET MARRIAGE AT 21 AFTER BOYFRIEND'S ALLEGED SHOCKING ULTIMATUM

"She said, 'Don't worry, you grow to love him.' I was like, 'Mom, that's not my generation,'" she said. "Her generation was like, 'Is he a good man? Will he provide?' There wasn't any of this, 'I have to be madly in love.' My parents were married for 59 years, so whatever they figured out, they figured out. But I still wanted to hold out for that falling in love thing."

Ultimately, Wilson did not go through with marrying the first man, knowing "marriage would not have sustained that relationship," and found love with Hanks after they reunited on set of "Volunteers" in 1984, tying the knot in 1988.

The "Now and Then" actress told Obama and her co-host and brother, Craig Robinson, when she "finally met Tom and fell in love with" Hanks, she had the feeling that "this is very, very different than what I had before."

When it comes to being a mom, Wilson said she wasn't sure she wanted to have children, but knew she "didn't wanna have children with the wrong people or person."

"Tom had two children," she said. "I already saw that he could be a good dad. So, I was like, 'OK, good, that's helpful. A little example here.'"

Hanks was already a father to Colin and Elizabeth, who he shares with his ex-wife, Samantha Lewes, and later welcomed sons Chet and Truman with Wilson.

Of his children, Colin and Chet have followed in Hanks and Wilson's footsteps, with Elizabeth pursuing a career as an author and journalist under the pen name E.A. Hanks and Truman focusing on other aspects of filmmaking.

Most recently, Chet has found success starring in "Running Point" alongside Kate Hudson, and Colin has appeared in a number of successful projects, including "Life In Pieces," "Fargo," "American Crime Story" and others.

item.title: Viagra could do more than advertised as study reveals surprising health superpower
item.description: Sildenafil, Viagra's active ingredient, may restrict cancer metastasis by limiting cancer cells' cholesterol access, a new study has found.
item.content:encoded:
Viagra could do more than give men a boost in the bedroom, as new research suggests it may have benefits for cancer patients.

The prescription medication, which is manufactured and distributed by Viatris, is commonly used to treat erectile dysfunction by increasing blood flow during sexual stimulation.

It was originally developed to treat high blood pressure and chest pain caused by reduced blood flow to the heart before researchers discovered its unexpected effect on erectile function during clinical trials.

PANCREATIC CANCER VACCINE SHOWS PROMISE IN FIRST HUMAN TRIAL, PREVENTING DISEASE IN HIGH-RISK PATIENTS

A new study published by the American Association for Cancer Research found that the pill may have properties that can prevent cancer from spreading.

Researchers at the Weizmann Institute of Science in Israel, led by Dr. Yarden Ariav in the lab of professor Ayelet Erez, found that Viagra’s active ingredient — sildenafil, a PDE5 inhibitor — may restrict cancer metastasis, or the formation of new tumors.

The team, which included scientists at the U.S. National Cancer Institute, analyzed human and mouse cancer cells, genetic experiments and 20 years of health data from 5 million members of Clalit Health Services, Israel's largest nonprofit healthcare provider and health insurer. They also examined how genes, proteins, fats, cholesterol and cellular energy interact.

The analysis revealed that sildenafil limits the cancer cell’s ability to make use of cholesterol, which is an important mechanism in how the cell breaks away from the primary tumor and migrates throughout the body, according to a press release from the American Committee for the Weizmann Institute of Science.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Sildenafil was found to block an enzyme called phosphodiesterase type 5, or PDE5, and increase the signaling molecule called cGMP, which dilates blood vessels – the feature that has made Viagra a successful treatment for erectile dysfunction.

According to the researchers, cGMP also binds to a protein that transports cholesterol within cells, reducing the cholesterol available for essential cellular functions. Cancer cells are "particularly vulnerable to this reduction in cholesterol supply," they noted.

Based on their findings, the researchers suggested that combining Viagra-related drugs with statins, which lower cholesterol, could help slow the spread of cancer by reducing tumor cells' access to both existing and newly produced cholesterol.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

"We have uncovered a new biological pathway that links a well-known signaling molecule to cholesterol regulation within cells and shown how this pathway can be harnessed to interfere with the ability of cancer cells to form metastases," Erez, senior researcher and dean of Weizmann’s Miriam and Aaron Gutwirth Medical School, commented in a statement.

"Beyond their therapeutic promise, our findings highlight that cancer biology is shaped not only by mutations in tumor cells, but also by the patient’s metabolic state and by medications they are already taking for other conditions."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The researcher added that this study "underscores the importance of treating the whole patient – not just the cancer – when tailoring the most effective therapy."

The study’s use of mouse models could pose a limitation to the final implications, as cancer treatment may not always translate similarly to humans, the researchers acknowledged.

The human evidence is also observational, which reveals an association instead of a proven cause and effect.

Fox News Digital reached out to the study authors and the medication's manufacturer for comment.

item.title: Fauci slapped with subpoena as COVID doc probed for 'profiting' off federal guidance
item.description: The subpoena seeks documents on Anthony Fauci's book deals, awards and alleged self-dealing tied to COVID-19 guidance that impacted Florida businesses.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: A top Florida official is slapping Anthony Fauci with a subpoena over alleged "profiting" from federal guidance that hurt businesses, residents.

Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier announced Wednesday he has issued an investigative subpoena against former National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Disease Director Anthony Fauci.

The subpoena is part of a state probe into Fauci’s awards, incentives and guidance that impacted Florida’s residents and their businesses during the coronavirus pandemic.

FAUCI'S FIFTH FUELS VOW TO HAUL HIM INTO COURT 'EVERY DAY' DESPITE BIDEN PARDON

The announcement comes after Uthmeier, along with Sen. Tommy Tuberville, R-Ala., pledged to have Fauci investigated at the state level following his Senate Homeland Security and Government Affairs Committee hearing last week when he pleaded the Fifth 111 times and references were made to his blanket federal pardon from former President Joe Biden.

"We issued a formal subpoena to Dr. Fauci under Florida state law, seeking a breadth of documents ranging to what he knew when he knew it, his doubts about the safety and efficacy of vaccines that he's out there promoting, and we're really focused in on his self-dealing," Uthmeier announced on Fox News.

"Evidence has come to light that he was trying to personally profit off of this. This is outside of his government duties, his official role: He's trying to pursue book deals, awards, get connected with high rollers that might help him come into millions and millions of dollars. This is wrong, and it could go towards a deceptive trade practice, fraud, public nuisance, you name it. I think there's many aspects of Florida law that now are implicated."

Uthmeier said the activities he is being subpoenaed over were revealed largely through his diary – several hundred pages of writings made on a federal server that Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., released last week.

FAUCI'S NEWLY RELEASED COVID DIARIES REVEAL BIZARRE FIXATION ON FAME AS PANDEMIC DEATHS MOUNTED

"We know one award in particular, he made $900,000 on that," he said, appearing to refer to Fauci receiving approximately that amount from the Dan David Prize from Tel Aviv University.

Uthmeier said that when a bureaucrat is issuing directives and mandates he is privately questioning while also deriving a profit from that work, it raises legal questions.

"It starts as a civil inquiry," Uthmeier said. "But we're going to tie in all aspects of Florida common law, things ranging from deceptive trade, fraud, public nuisance, nothing is off the table."

The subpoena asks for awards Fauci applied to, considered or received from any organization, including those within the state of Florida, relating to the pandemic.

FAUCI PRIVATELY TOOK CREDIT FOR COVID-19 LOCKDOWNS DESPITE PUBLIC DENIAL, NEWLY EXPOSED DIARY ENTRIES REVEAL

It also asks for information on professional opportunities offered to or considered by Fauci, as well as interactions and communications with Florida businesses, media outlets and communities regarding COVID-19 vaccination sites, social distancing and mask orders, and school closures.

A pair of other states expressed encouragement at the news.

West Virginia Attorney General JB McCuskey alleged Fauci’s refusal to answer Paul’s questions is "concerning" and that the American people deserve to know whether they were misled or "manipulated."

"Both my Office and I support Attorney General Uthmeier’s efforts to uncover the truth," McCuskey said in a statement obtained by Fox News Digital.

Louisiana Attorney General Liz Murrill added that the public "deserves answers to about a million questions related to the pandemic, its origins, and the government’s actions in response."

Murrill alleged Fauci had lied and said that "we just don’t know how much" so.

"But he lied about something as basic as keeping a diary. The truth will come out."

item.title: Terrifying 'human safaris' on display in shocking video that reveals depths of Russia's deadly campaign
item.description: Video shows a Russian drone stalking a vegetable vendor through a Kherson market before detonating near him, in what Zelenskyy calls a "safari."
item.content:encoded:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Russia of going "mad" following the release of a video showing a Ukrainian vegetable vendor being stalked by a Russian military drone before the drone exploded near him.

The incident occurred on Aug. 4 at a Kherson market located in Southern Ukraine. Footage released by the Kherson Regional Military Administration shows a drone hovering near a man standing beside a minibus before following him as he moves behind the bus. Moments later the drone dives toward the minibus and explodes near its front, detonating close to where the man is standing.

"A Russian drone deliberately hunted down a man selling vegetables and detonated right next to him," Zelenskyy wrote on X in a post including the video. "The Russians even admitted to the crime, showing zero regret and openly boasting about tormenting people. The man was wounded in the blast. Every single day, ordinary people in Kherson face these Russian "safaris."

MOSCOW BOMBING EXPOSES POTENTIAL SECURITY GAPS AROUND PUTIN'S MILITARY ELITE, EXPERT SAYS

The street vendor, identified as 52-year-old Yuriy, survived the near-fatal encounter, which Ukrainian authorities describe as part of a pattern of Russian drone attacks that track and target civilians — a practice they have dubbed "human safaris."

Speaking from a hospital bed, Yuriy told BBC that he and his wife were setting up their stall when he heard the drone buzzing nearby. His wife had run away, and the drone zeroed in on Yuriy, who pulled out vegetables to show that he did not have a weapon.

"It could see that I had tomatoes out, some cucumbers and eggplants laid out on the floor," Yuriy told BBC. "It even ducked under the umbrella when I was running away round the other side."

Ukraine's Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha called the attack a "barbaric war crime," demanding international intervention.

WHY TRUMP IS DOWNPLAYING REPORTS RUSSIA AND CHINA ARE HELPING IRAN

Zelenskyy argued that everyone should see the video to make clear what Russia is capable of, arguing that President Vladimir Putin won't stop with Ukraine.

"This is not just about Ukraine," Zelenskyy wrote. "Russia’s campaign against human life must be stopped here in Ukraine before it spreads further. Finland and Kazakhstan, the Baltic states and Poland, the countries of the South Caucasus, Romania, and Moldova — all should work together to ensure real security guarantees and bring Russia’s war to an end."


"Peace is needed, which requires cooperation among everyone in the world who truly values peace," Zelenskyy wrote.

Ukraine's Prosecutor General's Office says authorities have opened 5,303 criminal cases into drone attacks on civilian targets in the Kherson region. The office says the attacks have killed 287 civilians and wounded 2,549 others, including 41 children.

UKRAINE SEEKS MORE U.S. PATRIOT INTERCEPTORS AS BOMB SHELTER PROBE DEEPENS

Prosecutors said the attacks appeared to be part of a systematic campaign, with FPV drones repeatedly striking civilians in public places, homes, transport hubs and civilian vehicles, and in some cases launching follow-up attacks after emergency crews arrived.

The release of the chilling video comes a year after a one-year-old boy was killed by a Russian drone in the Kherson region while playing in his playpen in his grandmother's backyard.
